title: fix(net): send Sec-Fetch metadata on script fetch() and XHR
body:
Fixes #1292.

## Problem

Script-initiated requests (`fetch()`, `XMLHttpRequest`, and the module/resource loads that share `op_fetch_url`) went out without `Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Sec-Fetch-Mode`, or `Sec-Fetch-Dest`. The navigation path already built them in `fetch_with_profile_uncached`, but the script path did not.

Servers that trust Fetch Metadata for same-origin guards see the header missing and treat the request as cross-site, so a same-origin API call gets rejected (401 or a CSRF abort) even though the page and the endpoint share an origin.

Repro against a local endpoint that only accepts `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`:

```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/risk
401
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin" http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/risk
200
```

On a real page whose risk card fetches `/api/risk`, obscura 0.2.5 rendered "Risk metrics unavailable"; with this patch the card loads its data.

## Fix

Three helpers in `obscura-net` (`script_fetch_site`, `script_fetch_mode`, `script_fetch_dest`) mirror the navigation-path classification, and both script transports (the plain reqwest loop and the stealth client) set the headers on each hop.

Classification stays conservative:
- A differing origin reports `cross-site` rather than guessing `same-site` without the public suffix list. An over-broad `same-origin` would be a security regression; `cross-site` never overstates ambient trust.
- An empty or opaque (`null`) initiator reports `none`.
- `Sec-Fetch-Mode` maps the fetch() mode string: `navigate` -> `navigate`, `no-cors` -> `no-cors`, everything else (including `same-origin`) -> `cors`, matching `RequestMode::header_value`.
- `Sec-Fetch-Dest` reuses the same resource-type mapping as the navigation path (`ResourceRequest::destination`), so a document load reports `document`, a script `script`, an XHR/fetch `empty`, and so on.

Only `http`/`https` requests get the headers; other schemes are untouched.

## Tests

- `fetch_and_xhr_send_sec_fetch_metadata_headers` (obscura-js, render): a std-thread listener records the headers of a same-origin `fetch()`, an explicit `no-cors` `fetch()`, and an XHR, and asserts site/mode/dest on all three.
- `script_fetch_metadata_classifies_site_mode_and_dest` (obscura-net): unit coverage for the three helpers, including same-origin, cross-site, empty/opaque initiator, unparsable target, all four mode strings, and every resource type.

`cargo nextest run --release --features render -p obscura-js -p obscura-net --no-fail-fast` passes 886/886 locally.

title: render: keep `<picture>` inline, and let a transparent background flatten
body: ### What Each of these two defects shrinks a `width:100%` image inside a link to nothing. ```html ``` **`` was laid out as a block.** `ua_style()` lists the inline phrasing elements but leaves out `picture`, so it falls through to the block default. `` is a transparent wrapper around its `img`: the HTML rendering section gives it no `display`, and Chromium and Gecko both leave it inline. As a block inside the inline `` that usually wraps it, its width resolved against that inline and came out as 0px, which took the image's `max-width:100%` with it. A loaded image with a correct intrinsic size painted nothing. **A transparent background stopped an inline from flattening.** `is_flattenable_inline()` required `background_color.is_none()`. normalize.css ships `a{background-color:transparent}`, so on every site that uses it, every anchor was unflattenable. The anchor became a real box and so the percentage basis for its own children, and a `width:100%` replaced child inside it collapsed instead of filling the real containing block. A fully transparent background paints nothing, so it isn't a decoration that needs its own box. ### Fix - `ua_style("picture")` is inline. - `is_flattenable_inline()` treats a background whose alpha is 0 the same as no background. ### Not covered An anchor that also has a generated `::after` stays unflattenable for a good reason: a pseudo box needs its host. So that anchor still supplies the percentage basis, which CSS 2.1 §10.1 says an inline box must never do. That's a separate change. ### Verification - New tests in `style.rs`: `picture_is_an_inline_wrapper_not_a_block_box` and `a_transparent_background_is_not_an_inline_decoration`. - `cargo test --release -p obscura-render --features paint`, on top of `main` (v0.2.5): every test passes except `inline::tests::configured_font_directory_loads_nested_fonts_and_skips_symlinks`, which also fails on unmodified `main` because it depends on test order, and passes when run by itself.

title: docs: correct the top-level flag scope claim in the CLI reference
body:
## What changed

`docs/CLI-reference.md` opened with a blanket rule that is not true:

> Top-level flags apply to every subcommand.

`--storage-dir` is not global. It is declared on the `Serve` and `Fetch` variants of `Command`, and the top-level copy is read only on the `Mcp` path. This narrows the sentence to name that exception and says where to put the flag.

## Why

The page then lists `--storage-dir` in the top-level flag block, so the natural reading is that `obscura --storage-dir DIR serve` configures the storage directory for `serve`. It does not: `serve` and `fetch` each read their own field, which only gets a value when the flag appears after the subcommand. Top-level placement is accepted without any warning and has no effect on those two subcommands, which is the same silent-no-op shape reported for `--user-agent` in #1278.

## How this was verified

Read from `crates/obscura-cli/src/main.rs` on `main` (bd95294):

- `Args::storage_dir` is declared `#[arg(long)]` at line 48 — no `global = true`. The genuinely global top-level args are `verbose` (21), `proxy` (30), `stealth` (36), `obey_robots` (41) and `allow_private_network` (55).
- `storage_dir` is declared per subcommand on `Serve` (line 128) and `Fetch` (line 194). `Scrape` and `Mcp` do not declare it.
- The top-level value is read once, at line 443 (`let global_storage_dir = args.storage_dir.clone();`), and its only consumer is the `Mcp` arm at line 648, which sets `OBSCURA_STORAGE_DIR`. There is no other read of `global_storage_dir` in the file.

## Scope and relation to #1278 / #1279

This is a documentation correction only. It does not change CLI behavior and does not address the `--user-agent` routing problem in #1278, which is already covered by the open PR #1279. I deliberately kept `--user-agent` out of this change: #1279 makes that flag global, so a note saying the top-level copy is ignored would be wrong as soon as that PR lands. This `--storage-dir` exception is untouched by #1279 — that PR's patch contains no added or changed `storage_dir` line — so this note stays accurate either way.

Per CONTRIBUTING this counts as a small doc fix, so no linked issue is required.

## Validation

- Documentation-only change; no runtime, build, or rendering path is touched, so no code checks apply.
- Rendered-page output is unaffected.
- Confirmed the change is confined to one file and does not disturb the flag listing that follows it.

- [ ] Tests cover the failure or feature. Not applicable — no code change.

- [x] Public API or user-facing behavior changes are documented. This change corrects the documentation of existing behavior.

title: fix(net): gate file:// reads inside the loader
body:
## What changed

`fetch_file_url` read local files without any `--allow-file-access` check of its own. The gate lived only in its callers (Page navigation, the CDP handlers), so a new caller that fetched a URL directly would bypass it.

The loader now takes the flag and refuses `file://` when it is off, with `file:// access is disabled (requires --allow-file-access): <url>`. `ObscuraHttpClient` holds the flag as an `AtomicBool` because `BrowserContext` sets it after the client is already shared in an `Arc`; `StealthHttpClient` holds a plain field. `BrowserContext::set_allow_file_access` sets the context field and the client together, and `isolated_copy` carries it to the copy's client (server connections navigate through those copies). The existing caller-side checks and their error messages are untouched. `fetch --dump original file://...` builds its own client, so it opts in the same way `fetch` already does.

Fixes #857

title: fix(cli): make --user-agent a global flag

## What changed

Makes the top-level `--user-agent` a global flag and adds it to `scrape`.

Fixes #1278.

## Why

`Args::user_agent` was declared `#[arg(long)]` (not `global = true`) and no match arm read `args.user_agent`, so `obscura --user-agent X fetch URL` silently used the built-in default UA. `scrape` had no `--user-agent` of its own, so there was no way to set one there.

## Fix

- Mark `user_agent` `global = true`, mirroring `--proxy`, `--stealth`, and `--obey-robots`.
- Merge the global value with any subcommand-level `--user-agent` via a `merge_user_agent` helper (subcommand wins), matching `merge_proxy`.
- `scrape` forwards the resolved UA to its worker process via a new `OBSCURA_USER_AGENT` env var (same pattern as `OBSCURA_PROXY`).

## Tests

Added unit tests in `obscura-cli` covering the parse routing and merge precedence:
- `user_agent_before_subcommand_reaches_fetch`
- `subcommand_user_agent_wins_over_global`
- `scrape_accepts_global_user_agent`
- `merge_user_agent_prefers_command_value`

## Validation

Built `obscura` and ran it against a loopback server that echoes the `User-Agent` it receives.

```
# A: top-level flag before the subcommand (the bug)
obscura --allow-private-network --user-agent "TestUA/1.0" fetch $U --dump text
  before: Mozilla/5.0 (...) Chrome/143...   after: TestUA/1.0

# B: after the subcommand (already worked)
obscura --allow-private-network fetch --user-agent "TestUA/1.0" $U --dump text
  TestUA/1.0

# scrape (previously an "unexpected argument" parse error)
obscura --allow-private-network scrape $U --user-agent "ScrapeUA/9.9"
  server logged: GOT-UA: ScrapeUA/9.9

# default control (no flag) still sends the built-in UA
obscura --allow-private-network fetch $U --dump text
  Mozilla/5.0 (...) Chrome/143...
```

`cargo test -p obscura-cli --bins --no-default-features` → 60 passed, 0 failed (the 4 new tests included). `cargo build -p obscura-cli --bins` compiles clean.

title: fix(js): run javascript: URLs instead of fetching them
body:
## What changed

Fixes #1245.

`javascript:` URLs were treated like any other URL to fetch, which fails two ways:

1. `<iframe src="javascript:...">` reset the frame, sent the URL to `op_fetch_url`, got `blocked`, and left an empty placeholder. The script never ran. Now the frame keeps its initial about:blank realm (same-origin with the parent, like Chrome), the script runs there in a task, and a string result becomes the frame's document. The frame's `load` fires afterwards. A sandbox without `allow-scripts` runs nothing, and `document.open()` or `write()` on the frame before the script runs aborts it, like Chrome, so the common `src="javascript:''"` then `contentDocument.write(...)` pattern keeps what was written.
2. `location.href`/`assign`/`replace`, the `window.location` and `document.location` setters, and form submit passed `javascript:` URLs to `op_navigate`. Because `op_navigate` resolves the entered realm, a page assigning a frame's location queued the URL on the top-level page, and `Page.navigate` then failed with `Forbidden URL scheme 'javascript'`. These now run the script against the target document instead, and `op_navigate` drops `javascript:` URLs as a backstop.

## Validation

- New `crates/obscura-cdp/tests/javascript_iframe_src.rs`: the snippet from the issue, string vs non-string results, percent-decoding, sandboxing, the open/write abort, and a page that sends `javascript:` URLs during load through a frame's location, top-level `location.href` and a form action while `Page.navigate` succeeds.
- New `javascript_urls_run_instead_of_queueing_a_navigation` in `obscura-browser` page tests.
- All 4 new tests fail on main and pass here, with render and `--no-default-features`.
- `cargo nextest run --release --features render --no-fail-fast`: 2151 passed, 4 failed. Those 4 also fail on main for me on Windows, two of them only intermittently (`read_body_capped_reads_body_within_cap`, `intersection_observer_tracks_viewport_threshold_crossings`, `intersection_observer_clips_through_intermediate_overflow_ancestors`, `intersection_observer_element_root_uses_live_padding_box_and_scroll`).
- A real page that builds frames like this during load used to fail `Page.navigate` with the error above. It doesn't anymore.

## Rendering

Not applicable

## Performance

One `Map.size` check per DOM insertion and a counter on `document.write`. No change for other URLs. I didn't take measurements.

## Notes

- The iframe `load` event fires for every outcome, matching the existing blocked-fetch path. Chrome may skip it for a non-string result.
- Noticed but not changed here: since `op_navigate` uses the entered realm, `iframe.contentWindow.location.href = "https://..."` from the page navigates the whole page. That seems worth its own issue.

title: fix(cdp): report script request headers and post data on requestWillBeSent
body:
## What changed

Fixes #1246.

Two problems:

1. `Network.requestWillBeSent` for fetch/XHR never carried the request headers or body. The fetch op's network event had no request fields, the non-stealth completion rebuilt the event from scratch, and the CDP builders never set `hasPostData` or `postData`. The event now records the page's headers (after any `Fetch.continueRequest` override) and the body before the request goes out, for both transports. `postData` is included when the body is 64 KiB or smaller. Larger bodies only set `hasPostData`, which the protocol allows.
2. Without `--stealth` the event wasn't missing, it was late. Script network events were only published at the end of an autonomous pump turn, and a pending timer could hold that turn back. `process_cdp_message` now publishes queued network events right after dispatch, so the events of a fetch awaited inside `Runtime.evaluate` arrive before the command's response. History change events keep their current ordering.

Only the page's own headers are reported. Origin, Cookie and the User-Agent the transport adds are left for a `requestWillBeSentExtraInfo` follow-up, since stealth sets the UA inside wreq where the op can't see it.

## Validation

- New `js_fetch_request_reports_headers_and_post_data` in `js_fetch_emits_network_events.rs`: a POST with a custom header reports `X-Probe`, `Content-Type`, `hasPostData: true` and `postData`.
- New `server::tests::awaited_fetch_network_events_precede_the_command_response`: with a 60s timer pending, the event arrives before the evaluate response.
- Both fail on main.
- `cargo nextest run --release --features render -p obscura-cdp -E 'test(/js_fetch|awaited_fetch_network_events|network_events|runtime_network/)'`: 8 passed. Same filter with `--features render,stealth`: 13 passed. With `--no-default-features`: 9 passed.
- `cargo nextest run --release --features render --no-fail-fast`: 2149 passed, 4 failed. They're IntersectionObserver and body cap tests that also fail on main for me on Windows, two of them only intermittently (`read_body_capped_reads_body_within_cap`, `intersection_observer_tracks_viewport_threshold_crossings`, `intersection_observer_element_root_uses_live_padding_box_and_scroll`, `intersection_observer_clips_through_intermediate_overflow_ancestors`).
- Ran the repro from the issue against render and render,stealth builds. Headers, `hasPostData` and `postData` now arrive together with the evaluate result in both modes.

## Rendering

Not applicable

## Performance

Each script network event now holds the request headers and up to 64 KiB of body, and queued network events are synced once after each CDP command. I didn't take measurements.

title: fix(js): expose page built-ins through the worker global object
body:
## What changed

Fixes #1247.

Workers run in a plain scope object through `with (scope) { eval(source) }`, so built-ins were reachable as bare identifiers but not through the worker's global object. `self.Object` was `undefined` and `'Object' in self` was `false`. Obfuscated worker code that looks globals up through `self` failed with `Object is not defined`.

`self`, `globalThis` and the top-level `this` in a worker are now a proxy over the scope. Reads that miss the scope fall back to the page global, and writes stay in the worker. Message handlers are called with the same object so `this === self` still holds. Bare identifier lookup through `with` is unchanged.

This doesn't give workers their own realm. It only makes the existing scope behave more like a worker global for property lookups.

## Validation

- New `runtime::tests::worker_self_exposes_page_builtins`: checks `typeof self.Object`, `'Object' in self`, `typeof self.Uint8Array`, `typeof this.Object`, `self === globalThis`, and that a write to `self` doesn't leak to the page. It fails on main.
- `cargo nextest run --release --features render -p obscura-js -E 'test(/worker/)'`: 10 passed, including the existing worker tests. Same with `--no-default-features`.
- `cargo nextest run --release --features render --no-fail-fast`: 2143 passed, 9 failed while the machine was under heavy load. 6 of those pass on rerun (IntersectionObserver, rAF and loading timing tests). The other 3 fail on main for me on Windows too: `read_body_capped_reads_body_within_cap` and `intersection_observer_tracks_viewport_threshold_crossings` every time, and `intersection_observer_element_root_uses_live_padding_box_and_scroll` intermittently (3 of 5 runs on main).

title: fix(js): fire load and error for <link rel="preload">

## What changed

Fixes #1244.

A dynamically inserted `<link rel="preload">` was ignored because `_loadLinkedStylesheet` returned early for anything but `rel=stylesheet`, so the link never fired `load` or `error`. `relList.supports('preload')` reports `true`, so loaders that feature-detect it wait on the preload forever. React 19 does this for stylesheets, so a Next.js app router page that lazy loads a component with CSS never mounts it.

Preload and modulepreload links now fetch the resource for the supported `as` values (style, script, font, image, fetch) and fire `load` or `error`. Nothing is applied, so a preloaded stylesheet doesn't enter the cascade. Like Chrome, nothing is fetched when `as` is missing or unknown.

title: cdp(page): implement Page.close as an alias for Target.closeTarget
body:
Closes #1237.

## Problem

`obscura serve` (CDP mode) answered `Page.close` with:

```
WARN obscura_cdp::dispatch: CDP error for Page.close: Unknown Page method: close
{"error":"Error -32601: Unknown Page method: close"}
```

`Page.close` is the DevTools protocol's page-teardown method and the primary
teardown path for Puppeteer-style clients. A client that respects the response
could never confirm a close, so ephemeral-session cleanup logged a spurious
`renderer may be orphaned` warning per page (11 WARNs for a 6-page burst) and
the page was only freed when the whole connection dropped.

## Fix

`Page.handle` and `Target.handle` take the same arguments, so `Page.close`
resolves its own session's page id and delegates to the existing
`Target.closeTarget` arm:

```rust
"close" => {
    let target_id = ctx
        .get_session_page(session_id)
        .map(|page| page.id.clone())
        .ok_or("Page.close requires a session with an attached page")?;
    crate::domains::target::handle(
        "closeTarget",
        &json!({ "targetId": target_id }),
        ctx,
        session_id,
    )
    .await
}
```

Delegating rather than reimplementing keeps the existing teardown behaviour
intact: the `Target.detachedFromTarget` and `Target.targetDestroyed` events
still fire exactly once, the page is still released, and only the session's own
page is touched. Clients that already use `Target.closeTarget` (the documented
workaround) are unaffected.

## Tests

Two tests added next to the existing `printToPDF` / `captureScreenshot`
fallthrough regressions:

- `page_close_aliases_target_close_target`: returns `{"success": true}`,
  removes only its own page, stops resolving that session, and emits
  `Target.targetDestroyed` for its own target.
- `page_close_without_a_page_session_errors`: a descriptive error, not the
  generic catch-all.

Both fail without the new arm (verified by temporarily disabling it) and pass
with it.

`cargo nextest run -p obscura-cdp`: 193 passed, 1 failed,
`iframe_document_dispatches_registered_listeners` (SIGABRT). That one also
fails on a clean `main` in this environment, so it is pre-existing and
unrelated.

## Note

The `DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot` schema gap mentioned in #1237 is untouched
here. It needs a real layer tree to populate `stackingContexts`, so it is left
as the descriptive error it already returns.

body:
Fixes #1207.

`permissions.query({name: 'geolocation'})` answered `prompt` while `getCurrentPosition` handed out coordinates. Chrome cannot produce that combination, so the page's own permission state was enough to tell a real browser from this one.

The permission is now granted exactly when coordinates were configured for the page (`OBSCURA_GEOLOCATION`):

title: fix(js): retry module fetches and report their real body size
body:
## What changed

A module load is a single round trip with no retry. One transient socket failure therefore strands the whole graph: a `<script type="module">` never runs, or a lazy `import()` throws `error sending request` into the page, and the document stays on its boot splash with an empty root and an empty console. Nobody can tell an engine fault from an app fault from that symptom.

Two changes in `crates/obscura-js/src/module_loader.rs`:

- `fetch_module_with_retry` retries three times with a short backoff. The `ResourceRequest` is rebuilt per attempt because a retry closure cannot move a captured value out. The retry only covers transport errors; a non-2xx response still fails immediately, as before.
- A module response never went through the path that records a completed response, so every module script was reported as 0 B and read as an empty body. The loader now publishes the decoded size and status onto the event the request side already created.

Relates to #1222. That issue also reports module scripts being skipped on load, which this does not address; the retry covers the failure mode, not the accounting of an empty result.

## Validation

- Fixture: one classic script, one `<script type="module">`, and a dynamic `import()` inside the module. Before, the module pair intermittently never ran. After, all three report their values on the first load, across repeated runs.
- The retry helper is exercised by every module fetch, so a transient failure can be simulated by dropping the first attempt; the graph recovers instead of stranding.
- `cargo check --workspace --features render --all-targets` and the focused nextest filters pass on an arm64 runner.
- Not run here: the obstacle course, stealth and no-render configurations, which a maintainer's `PR checks` run covers.

## Rendering

Not applicable

## Performance

Three attempts only on the error path; a successful module load does one fetch exactly as before. The added work per successful load is one `len()` on an already-decoded string and one reverse scan of the network event list, which is bounded by the retained event count.

title: net: fetch missing intermediates from AIA caIssuers
body:
Fixes #1216.

## Changes

On an unknown-issuer failure, fetch the missing intermediate from the leaf's AIA `caIssuers` URL (DER, PEM or PKCS#7), offer it to the verifier as an untrusted intermediate only, and retry, for up to 3 missing intermediates.

- **Verification is unchanged.** A fetched certificate is never a trust anchor; it only helps build a path to an already-trusted root, and hostname, expiry and signature checks are untouched. A fetched bundle that does not contain the direct issuer is ignored and negatively cached.
- **Fetching is constrained.** URL and every redirect hop go through `validate_url` and `SsrfGuardResolver` (private addresses refused unless allowed), plain HTTP is allowed as in browsers, 64 KiB cap, 5 s timeout, at most 3 redirects, configured proxy honoured, and the AIA fetch never triggers AIA itself.
- **Cache.** Bounded in-memory cache (64 URLs, FIFO) with 5-minute negative entries, so a site costs one AIA fetch per process.
- **Default client (reqwest/rustls).** The webpki verifier is wrapped in an `AiaVerifier` that retries with cached intermediates on `UnknownIssuer` and records the presented chain; `send_with_aia` fetches the issuer and retries. Used by the HTTP client and by JS `fetch` (request and CORS preflight).
- **Stealth client (wreq/BoringSSL).** wreq reports only `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED`, so after a verified request fails the client reads the server's chain with one verification-off `HEAD /` (same emulation, proxy and SSRF resolver, no cookies; only the certificates are used), fetches the intermediate when the issuer is not a bundled root, rebuilds the client with the intermediates in its `tls_cert_store`, and retries. No `tls_options` are set, so the TLS fingerprint is unchanged.
- **Dependencies.** No new crates in `Cargo.lock`: obscura-net gains direct dependencies on `rustls` (default features off; `ring`, `std`, `tls12`), `webpki-roots`, the workspace `base64`, and, under `stealth` only, `webpki-root-certs` (a wreq store replaces its bundled roots, so the store is rebuilt from them).

New module `crates/obscura-net/src/aia.rs` (minimal DER reader, AIA extraction, PKCS#7/PEM parsing, fetch and cache).

## Testing

Live, both clients, all four release builds: `incomplete-chain.badssl.com` loads; `untrusted-root`, `expired`, `wrong.host` and `self-signed` still fail; `badssl.com` loads.

- Unit tests: AIA URL extraction; DER/PEM/PKCS#7 parsing incl. garbage and truncated input; cache bound and negative expiry; a bundle without the direct issuer is ignored; SSRF refusal of loopback, metadata and `file://` URLs; size cap, status handling and redirect bound.
- Integration `tests/aia_incomplete_chain.rs` (local root, intermediate and leaf; HTTPS server omitting the intermediate; local HTTP AIA server), for each client: completes via one AIA fetch and serves the second request from cache; a 404 on the AIA URL fails; an impostor intermediate with the right name but an untrusted issuer stays rejected and is not refetched.
- `cargo nextest run --release`: obscura-net 136/136 (default) and 151/151 (stealth); obscura-net + obscura-js with render 804/804. All four release configurations build; obstacle course 33/33 on each.

## Limitations

The stealth path needs one extra verification-off `HEAD` to read the chain, only after a verified failure. With custom roots (`SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR`) its chain filter is skipped and AIA is always tried. The intermediate's own AIA is followed only within the 3-round bound.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); I reviewed the change and ran the checks above.

body:
## What changed

Resolves #1157.

This pull request implements comprehensive persistent storage under `--storage-dir`:

1. **Persistent `localStorage` Disk Sync:**
   - Flushes origin-scoped key-value stores to `<storage-dir>/localStorage/<sanitized_origin>.json` on modification.

   - Implements `window.caches` (`CacheStorage`) and `window.Cache` (`put`, `match`, `delete`, `keys`).

title: perf(js, dom): cut bridge and bootstrap overhead on DOM mutation paths
body:
Fixes #1155

Draft: this overlaps #1142 and #1111, which touch the same insertion paths in `bootstrap.js` and `ops.rs`. #1142 removes the IntersectionObserver MutationObserver that the first commit here makes lazy. I will rebase onto them once they land and drop what they already cover.

Reduces the per-call cost of DOM mutations and hot reads from page JS. No behavior change intended; all existing tests pass unchanged.

## Changes

- `perf(js)`: create an element's style declaration on first use; attach the internal IntersectionObserver MutationObserver only while an IntersectionObserver exists; one shared native query for the two insertion scans, cached per `_domMutationEpoch`.
- `perf(dom)`: composite ops `append_child_x`, `insert_before_x`, `remove_child_x`, `set_text_el` do the mutation and its follow-up queries in one `op_dom` call, through `op_dom_inner` so render invalidation is unchanged. `op_dom_nav` serves parent, child, sibling, nodeType and isConnected on the fast-call path. Cached `parentNode` survives unrelated insertions. The handlers borrow nodes instead of cloning them.
- `perf(js)`: dense array for the wrapper cache; created elements share an empty attribute marker until the first write; composite `innerHTML` set when no observer or stylesheet/named content is involved.
- `perf(js)`: wrapping an element is one numeric call (node type plus wrapper class code); `getAttribute`, `tagName`, `textContent`, `innerHTML` and friends return raw strings instead of JSON.
- `perf(js)`: flat `[name, value]` array for tracked attributes of created elements.

The composite paths fall back to the previous code whenever MutationObservers exist, or the affected subtree holds `<style>`/`<link>` or id/name elements, so stylesheet and window named property bookkeeping is unchanged.

## Measurements

No-render release build, min of 7 interleaved runs, 20,000 operations each, `main` vs this branch:

| operation | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| createElement | 148 ms | 45 ms |
| appendChild | 175 ms | 62 ms |
| textContent= (empty element) | 78 ms | 36 ms |
| parentNode | 16 ms | 1 ms |
| className= | 56 ms | 49 ms |
| innerHTML read | 16 ms | 10 ms |

Fixes #1151

## Changes

- Enable reqwest's `http2` feature, with Chrome-sized flow-control windows (6 MiB per stream, 15 MiB per connection). - `start_script_fetches()` runs right after `init_js` and spawns external script downloads into a `JoinSet` (16 at a time), so they overlap the stylesheet wave. The set is dropped, and its tasks aborted, on the next navigation.
- `script_body()` waits only for that script's own download instead of a barrier on all fetches. An async script that has not arrived when the parser reaches it runs after the parser-blocking and defer scripts instead of holding them up, which the spec allows.

title: fix(dom): follow the DOM spec for mutations, observers and node documents
body:
## What changed

Fixes #1141.

DOM and CSSOM conformance fixes, found by a 22-file WPT subset (selectors, DOM mutation, MutationObserver, computed style, IntersectionObserver) and checked against a wider 837-file WPT set. Every fix implements the spec behavior in general. Nothing is keyed to test names or hosts.

- **Pre-insertion validity.** `appendChild`, `insertBefore`, `replaceChild`, `append`, `prepend`, `before`, `after`, `replaceWith`, `replaceChildren` and `Range.insertNode` share one check that runs in the spec's order. Non-Node arguments throw `TypeError`. Document child constraints are enforced. A new native op, `is_host_including_inclusive_ancestor`, reuses the tree's bounded cycle walk.
- **Mutation records.**
  - One `childList` record per insertion, with `previousSibling` and `nextSibling`.
  - A move queues a removal record on the old parent.
  - `replaceChild`, `replaceChildren`, `textContent` and `normalize` produce the spec's records.
  - Attribute records carry `attributeNamespace`, and `removeAttribute` and the `*NS` variants queue them.
  - `MutationRecord` is a real interface.
- **MutationObserver.**
  - Option validation and implied options follow the spec, and re-observing a target replaces its options.
  - `oldValue` is delivered only when requested, and `attributeFilter` is applied.
  - Callbacks run in one microtask, in creation order, with the observer as `this`.
- **Range.** `deleteContents`, `extractContents`, `cloneContents`, `insertNode` and `surroundContents` are implemented; they were no-op stubs. Ancestor checks use a native upward walk, which also speeds up the existing boundary comparisons.
- **Node documents.**
  - `createHTMLDocument` and `createDocument` return real `Document` nodes with their own native tree root.
  - `ownerDocument` follows the tree root, including `DOMParser` and iframe documents.
  - `importNode` and `adoptNode` set the node document.
  - Exceptions, node lists and argument errors of iframe-document nodes use the frame's `DOMException`, `NodeList` and `TypeError`.
- **Post-connection order.** When several nodes are inserted at once, their post-connection steps run in tree order after the insertion. A script inserted before an iframe therefore sees the iframe without a content window, as in Chromium.
- **CSSOM.** `@media` and `@supports` are exposed as `CSSMediaRule` and `CSSSupportsRule` with nested rules. `insertRule` and `deleteRule` on them resync the sheet incrementally. CSSOM rule changes invalidate cached computed style.
- **getComputedStyle.** An element outside any document returns an empty declaration, matching Chromium. Elements in `display: none` iframes and non-slotted light DOM keep Chromium's behavior, which deliberately does not follow the spec.
- **Observers.**
  - `IntersectionObserver` and `ResizeObserver` callbacks get the observer as `this`.
  - `IntersectionObserverEntry` is an interface.
  - `isIntersecting` honors thresholds, as in Chromium.
  - A removed target reports empty `rootBounds`.
- **Layout (`obscura-render`).** Inline-blocks whose in-flow children are all blocks now lay them out as a block: the children stack and stretch, where before they shared a flex row and auto widths collapsed to 0. Formatting whitespace around those children no longer takes space.
- **Interface shapes.** The new interfaces match Chromium's: string tags, illegal constructors, constructor lengths and non-enumerable globals. `Element.webkitMatchesSelector` is added.
- **Performance changes in the same PR.**
  - The document-wide MutationObserver that only scheduled intersection updates is removed. Every mutating DOM command already schedules them.
  - Mutation records and IntersectionObserver entries keep their state in private fields, and their node lists and siblings are created only when read.
  - Siblings are read in one native call (`sibling_nids`), and subtree observers match through a native ancestor walk (`is_inclusive_ancestor`).

13 new focused tests are in `crates/obscura-js/src/runtime.rs` and `crates/obscura-dom/src/tree.rs`.

## Validation

On this branch (`2f6e09a` plus this commit), x86_64 Linux, Rust 1.94.1:

- **WPT subset** (22 files, WPT `8b6e09b`): 69/169 on `main` to **165/169** on this branch, with 0 regressions. Chromium also passes 165/169, and this branch passes the same 165 subtests. The 4 subtests Chromium fails are deliberately left at Chromium's behavior (`getComputedStyle` in `display: none` iframes and on non-slotted light DOM).
- **nextest:** release `--features render,stealth` passes 1922/1922 (1909/1909 on `main`). The 13 new tests run only on this branch.

The remaining gates ran on a fork base: `main` plus five unrelated changes that are open here as #1111, #1117, #1118, #1121 and #1126. This pull request does not depend on them. Base and this change were compared on that same base:

- **Wider WPT set** (837 files in `dom/nodes`, `dom/ranges`, `css/cssom` and `intersection-observer`):

  | Build | Subtests passed | Incomplete harnesses |
  |---|---|---|
  | base | 34,646 | 107 |
  | this change | **50,655** | **88** |
  | Chromium | 61,147 | 7 |

  0 subtests went from pass to fail; 16,009 went from fail to pass.
- **All four release configurations** build, and nextest passes in render, render+stealth and no-render.
- **Obstacle course:** identical on both builds. With the corrected `observer-intersection` fixture both score 33/33; with the original fixture both score 32/33.
- **Puppeteer, Playwright, CDP, HTTP/2, resource and client-isolation controls:** all pass.

## Rendering

- **Deterministic render fixtures** (69 fixtures, 207 captures): pixels are identical between base and this change.
- **Representative real-site suite** (15 framework-heavy sites, top and bottom against Chromium): 12 of 15 are pixel-identical at both positions. The small differences on porkbun.com, MDN and bulma.io change sign with capture order, which points to live content.
- **Real-world corpus** (98 live pages, ABBA): base 85 and 86, this change 87 and 87. No page regressed; npr.org now renders.

## Stealth and fingerprints

- **Fingerprint controls:** no value differs systematically between builds.
- **DOM/CSSOM surface probe against Chromium:** this change matches 47 of 50 surface values, against 13 for the base. It introduces no new mismatch. The new interfaces (`MutationRecord`, `IntersectionObserverEntry`, `CSSMediaRule`, `CSSSupportsRule`, `CSSConditionRule`) have Chromium's string tags, illegal constructors, constructor lengths and non-enumerable globals.

## Performance

Paired and interleaved: 5 rounds per cell at 1 and 10 browsers, CPU through 8 s after load, idle host.

- **CPU** on the medium, complex and MutationObserver-heavy fixtures is within the noise floor. RSS is about 2% lower.
- **Fixed cost:** about +2 ms of CPU per page process, measured with microsecond per-process CPU over 60 ABBA pairs (+2.3 ms on a 30 ms page, +2.1 ms on a 107 ms page). It comes from the 3.5% larger startup snapshot and first-call compilation of the new functions.

- [x] I checked for CPU, latency, and memory regressions. The fixed ~2 ms per-process cost is documented above.
- [x] Public API or user-facing behavior changes are documented.

title: fix: report the loaded document for POST navigations
body:
## What changed

Fixes #1124.

Two problems in how native form POST navigations were reported over CDP. In both cases the POST was sent once and the result page loaded; only the reporting was wrong.

- The Document network event of a navigation recorded the requested URL and a fixed `GET` method. After a redirect the page URL is the final URL, so CDP found no document for the navigation and clients such as Playwright got no navigation response (for example after a POST answered with 303). A POST without a redirect was reported as `GET`. The event now records the final URL and the method of the final request. Because the response does not say whether a redirect was 301/302/303 or 307/308, a redirected navigation reports `GET`.
- Page-initiated navigations (form submissions, script navigations) were sent to the first session found in an unordered map. With an additional session attached to the page, such as a Playwright CDP session, the navigation events could go to that session and the page client timed out or saw no response. The session is now chosen deterministically: the one that enabled lifecycle events, then Runtime, then the lowest session id.

title: fix(js): implement checkVisibility() and inherit computed visibility
body:
## What changed

`Element.checkVisibility()` was a stub that always returned `true`. It now follows the CSSOM View algorithm:

- `false` when the element is disconnected, has `display: contents`, or it or a flattened-tree ancestor has `display: none`.
- `opacityProperty` / `checkOpacity`: `false` when it or an ancestor has `opacity: 0`.
- `visibilityProperty` / `checkVisibilityCSS`: `false` when its computed `visibility` is not `visible`.

Box existence comes from `display`, not geometry, because some visible inline elements report 0x0 rects (#722). Render builds answer in one native call (`op_check_visibility`, `PreparedRender::check_visibility`) from the retained cascade. No-render builds read inline declarations, which is all `getComputedStyle()` reflects there.

While verifying this I found that render builds reported only an element's own `visibility` from `getComputedStyle()`, so children of a `visibility: hidden` parent read as `visible`. The renderer resolved inheritance only into its paint-culling flag. It now also stores the resolved value (`visibility_hidden_computed`) and `getComputedStyle()` reports it. The own value is kept because animation re-sampling needs it.

`content-visibility: hidden` is not consulted. The renderer does not implement it and paints that content, so `checkVisibility()` reports what Obscura shows. Chrome returns `false` there.

Fixes #1067.

## Validation

- Issue repro with a render release build: `[false,false]`, matching Chrome (was `[true,true]`). Stylesheet-driven `display: none`, inherited `visibility: hidden`, a child restored with `visibility: visible`, `opacity: 0` ancestors and `display: contents` also match Chrome.
- New tests: `element_check_visibility_follows_css_boxes_and_options` (obscura-js, passes with and without `render`), `computed_visibility_reports_inherited_value` and `check_visibility_uses_ancestor_display_opacity_and_computed_visibility` (obscura-render). The renderer visibility test fails without the fix.
- `cargo nextest run --release --features render --no-fail-fast`: 1773/1780. The 7 failures reproduce identically on `main` when rerun alone (`render_resource_loads_share_one_page_wide_concurrency_limit`, `timers_inside_a_fixed_wait_observe_bytes_that_land_during_it`, `a_miss_created_inside_an_awaited_expression_loads_during_the_wait`, `mcp_client::test_evaluate` fail on both; the other 3 pass on both in isolation).
- No-render `cargo nextest run --release -p obscura-render`: the same 29 layout tests fail on `main` and on this branch.
- All four release configurations build (render, render+stealth, no-render, no-render+stealth).
- Obstacle course: 32/33 on both `main` and this branch. `observer-intersection` fails on both (`expected 'io:50', got ''`), so it is unrelated to this change.

## Rendering

Not applicable. Paint still uses `effectively_invisible`, which is unchanged. The new field only affects what `getComputedStyle().visibility` reports.

## Performance

`checkVisibility()` was a constant `true`, so any real check costs something. Measured per call with release render builds (`performance.now()` loops, 3 to 5 interleaved runs):

| Page | `checkVisibility()` | `getBoundingClientRect()` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 elements | 2 to 3 us | 10 to 31 us |
| 1550 elements, depth 31 | 51 to 56 us | 52 to 82 us |

The cost does not depend on ancestor depth. On large pages it is the same fixed native-call overhead `getBoundingClientRect()` pays. An earlier JS version that walked `getComputedStyle()` per ancestor cost about 4 ms per call at depth 31, which is why this uses a native op. Results are not cached, because CSS animations and media changes can alter visibility without a DOM mutation. The renderer change adds one bool assignment per element in the inheritance pass.

## Checklist

- [x] The change is focused and does not remove existing behavior without justification.
- [x] Tests cover the failure or feature.
- [x] Existing tests pass, including render and no-render configurations when affected.
- [x] I checked for CPU, latency, and memory regressions.
- [ ] Public API or user-facing behavior changes are documented.

## Summary
- `parse_http_date` in `crates/obscura-net/src/cookies.rs` had no bounds on the parsed `day` or `year` fields from a Set-Cookie `expires` attribute.

title: fix(js): give each HTML element interface its own brand
body:
Fixes #1001

Most HTML element interfaces are aliases of `Element`, so `div instanceof HTMLIFrameElement` answered true for every element and every interface. style-loader's `addStyles` checks whether its insert target is an iframe, concluded `<head>` was one, read `head.contentDocument.head`, threw, cached `null`, and reported `Couldn't find a style target` — so a webpack-built application could not install a single stylesheet. Reproduction and the Chrome comparison are in #1001.

## The change

`_brandHtmlElementInterfaces()` in `bootstrap.js` gives 33 interfaces a real brand:

- **Prototype identity is preserved.** Each interface keeps `Element.prototype` as its `prototype`, so `HTMLDivElement.prototype.foo = …` still patches the prototype real elements use, exactly as the alias did.
- **`instanceof` answers from the tag name** via `Symbol.hasInstance`, gated on the XHTML namespace so a foreign-namespace element with a colliding local name does not match.
- **Element construction is untouched.** `_elementClassFor` still hands out `Element`, nothing re-wraps existing nodes, and the renderer sees no change. This is deliberately not the "real subclass per interface" refactor: that one would have to move every interface through `_elementClassFor` and `_wrap`, which is a much larger and riskier change than the bug needs.
- **Real subclasses are skipped** by the `globalThis[name] !== Element` test, so `HTMLFormElement`, `HTMLTextAreaElement`, `HTMLSlotElement`, `HTMLImageElement` and the media elements are untouched — and if one of the remaining 33 grows behaviour later, this code steps aside automatically.

`HTMLElement` and `HTMLUnknownElement` are intentionally not in the table: the first matches every HTML element, and the second matches exactly the tags no other interface claims, which needs the full known-element list rather than a tag list of its own.

The `HTMLSlotElement` block right above this code documents the same bug for one tag — it needed a real subclass because it needed `assignedNodes()`, i.e. behaviour. These need only identity.

## Tests

Two new tests in `crates/obscura-js/src/runtime.rs`:

- `html_element_interfaces_have_distinct_brands` — six negative brands that all used to answer true (`head instanceof HTMLIFrameElement`, `div instanceof HTMLAnchorElement`, `input instanceof HTMLSelectElement`, …), the positive brands, that `HTMLElement` still matches any element, that the real subclasses still work, that patching `HTMLDivElement.prototype` still reaches a live `<div>`, and that `new HTMLDivElement()` throws `TypeError` as in a browser.
- `style_loader_insert_target_is_not_mistaken_for_an_iframe` — reproduces `style-loader/lib/addStyles.js`'s `getElement` + insert path, including its `memo` cache, and asserts the stylesheet lands in `<head>` with a readable rule. It throws on an unbranded build.

## Verification

| Configuration | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `--features render` | ✅ |
| `--features render,stealth` | ✅ |
| `--no-default-features` | ✅ |
| `--no-default-features --features stealth` | ✅ |

- `cargo nextest run --release --features render -p obscura-js` — `514 tests run: 513 passed, 1 failed` at `--test-threads 6`. That one failure, `ops::tests::read_body_capped_rejects_oversized_streamed_body`, is flaky on this machine independent of this change: it fails the same way on a tree with this commit stashed, and passes 3/3 when run alone. At the default thread count on a 24-core box a second one joins it, `runtime::tests::intersection_observer_clips_through_intermediate_overflow_ancestors`; it also passes alone and at `--test-threads 6`. Both look like host contention rather than assertions about this change — happy to dig further if you see them in CI.
- `cargo nextest run --release --features render -p obscura-cdp -p obscura-browser` — `307 tests run: 307 passed, 3 skipped`
- Obstacle course: 32/33. The only failure is `observer-intersection` (`expected 'io:50', got ''`), which is #671 — it fails on `main` and, per that issue, in headless Chrome identically. Unchanged by this branch.

## Effect on a real page, and what this does not fix

On a production Angular + AngularJS console (webpack-built, style-loader in the bundle), **this fix and #1000 together** take the page from unusable to fully rendered — 33 DOM nodes and a blank screenshot become 151 nodes, three real form controls, and a correctly laid out, branded sign-in page. Playwright's locator layer becomes usable there too: `page.fill()` and `locator.click()` resolve and dispatch instead of timing out on actionability.

To be clear about attribution between the two: **this PR alone is not enough for that page.** Without #1000, zone.js still cannot find `MutationObserver.prototype.observe` and Angular's router rejects its first transition before styling matters. The two are independent bugs on independent code paths — this one is worth landing on its own merit (style-loader is common, and the brand semantics are simply wrong today), but it is not the whole story for that app.

Two further layers are still in the way on that page, both out of scope here and not yet filed:

```
Worker error: importScripts is not defined
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'readyState')
```

title: Add table/select DOM APIs and CJK font fallback to the renderer
body:
## What

Two independent fixes, both needed to render real-world Chinese portal pages.

### 1. Table / select / option DOM API family (bootstrap.js)

`HTMLTableElement`, `HTMLTableRowElement`, `HTMLTableCellElement`,
`HTMLTableSectionElement` and `HTMLSelectElement` were plain `Element`
aliases, so pages calling `table.insertRow()` / `row.insertCell()` /
`select.options.add(option)` / `new Option(...)` got "is not a function"
or "Option is not defined". Sina's news frontend (TabSwitchController)
trips exactly these on its homepage.

Adds, per the WHATWG HTML spec:

- Table: `insertRow`, `deleteRow`, `createTHead/TBody/TFoot/Caption`,
  `deleteTHead/TFoot/Caption`, `tHead`, `tFoot`, `tBodies`, `rows`, `caption`
- Row: `insertCell`, `deleteCell`, `cells`, `rowIndex`, `sectionRowIndex`
- Section: `insertRow`, `deleteRow`, `rows`
- Select: `options` (new `HTMLOptionsCollection` with `add`/`remove`),
  `selectedIndex`, `selectedOptions`, `value`, `length`, `add`, `remove`,
  `item`, `namedItem`, `multiple`, `size`
- `HTMLOptionElement` (no custom constructor; see gotcha below) and the
  `Option()` constructor global, following the existing `Image()` pattern
- Tag dispatch for OPTION/SELECT/TABLE/TBODY/THEAD/TFOOT/TR/TD/TH/CAPTION
  in both `_elementClassFor` and `_elementClassForKnownName`

Implementation note (non-obvious): an element subclass must NOT build its
own native node in a custom constructor. `createElement` has already
allocated the nid; constructing a second node leaves the appended node and
the JS wrapper pointing at different nids, so `options[i]`/`value` then
read the wrong node. Hence `HTMLOptionElement` has no custom constructor
and `Option()` goes through `document.createElement('option')`.

### 2. CJK font fallback (paint.rs)

The renderer only embeds Liberation/DejaVu faces, so every CJK codepoint
painted as tofu — a screenshot of news.sina.com.cn was unreadable boxes.
Adds:

- `contains_cjk()` covering the CJK ranges (radicals, punctuation,
  kana, bopomofo, Ext-A, URO, compat ideographs, fullwidth forms)
- `font_bytes_for_text()`: runs containing CJK switch to a system
  TrueType fallback loaded once via `OnceLock` (leaked for process
  lifetime). Candidate order: DroidSansFallbackFull, then wqy-zenhei.
  ab_glyph only rasterizes glyf outlines, so .ttc collections and CFF/OTTO
  faces (e.g. NotoSansCJK) are detected by sfnt tag and skipped.
- Latin-only runs keep the existing embedded-font path and metrics
  untouched.

## Verification

- `insertRow`/`insertCell` round-trip: rows/cells/textContent correct
- `new Option("a","1")`, `select.options.add(...)`: `options.length`,
  `selectedIndex`, `select.value`, `option.index` all correct
- news.sina.com.cn: `fetch --timeout 90 --wait-until domcontentloaded`
  now loads (previously timed out at the 30s default), dumps
  text/markdown, and screenshots with readable Chinese (verified by a
  vision model reading the rendered nav text off the PNG)
- Remaining console errors on Sina are Sina's own (references to element
  ids absent from their HTML) and third-party ad fetch failures

title: Add a --platform flag to pick the stealth identity OS
body:
## Problem

When --stealth is on, the browser identity is hardcoded to a Windows Chrome 145 fingerprint. The User-Agent header, the sec-ch-ua-platform header, and the navigator values all claim Windows/Win32 even when the binary is running on a Mac or a Linux box. Fingerprint checks can cross-check the claimed OS family against the one the connection actually comes from, so a Windows identity exiting a macOS kernel is a signal by itself.

There was no way to pick a different identity. The values were constants in obscura-net and the wreq client was built with Platform::Windows unconditionally.

## Fix

I added a StealthPlatform type (windows / macos / linux) in obscura-net and carried it through BrowserContext. The wreq emulation profile and the JS navigator values now read from it, so the wire headers and the navigator agree on one OS.

There is a new global --platform flag:

    obscura --stealth --platform linux fetch https://example.com

It applies to fetch, serve, scrape, mcp, and the bare CDP command. Scrape workers read `OBSCURA_STEALTH_PLATFORM` (the same way `OBSCURA_STEALTH` is forwarded today) and serve workers take a --platform argument, so the workers build the same identity as the parent process. The library side gets a BrowserConfig.stealth_platform field and a builder method.

In non-stealth builds the flag is accepted but does nothing, which is the same behavior --stealth has today.

The default is the host OS, since claiming a different OS family than the one the traffic exits from is itself a signal. This changes the default stealth identity on macOS builds from the old hardcoded Windows to macOS.

## Testing

- nextest full gate and the stealth suites pass, except a few browser timing tests that flake on main too (I checked on a clean tree) and one that needs OBSCURA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK=1, which CI already sets.
- obstacle course: 32/33 on both builds; the observer-intersection stage fails the same way without this change, so that one is pre-existing.
- wire check: fetched a header echo endpoint with each platform value and confirmed the UA and sec-ch-ua-platform on the wire. Same for the worker path, and an invalid value errors out with a clear message.

title: Expose bounded native downloads and transport diagnostics over CDP
body:
## What changed

Remote CDP clients need to retrieve file bytes through Obscura's native transport while retaining the selected browser context's cookies and proxy. Add `Obscura.download` and `Obscura.getTransportInfo`, with the CLI stealth feature propagated to CDP. This follows the [proposal on #360](https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura/issues/360#issuecomment-5654841182); it does not claim to implement reception streaming or the entirety of that issue.

`download` performs a native GET, buffers the bounded decoded response, then exports it through existing chunked `IO.read` / `IO.close` handles. Limits are 1–33,554,432 bytes and 1–60,000 milliseconds. It requires compiled and active stealth, uses native URL/DNS/redirect checks, and rejects non-HTTP schemes and embedded URL credentials. Existing per-connection stream limits and connection teardown bound retained data. The client still validates status/MIME and controls exported-file expiry.

`getTransportInfo` distinguishes compile support from runtime activation and reports transport, UA/platform, proxy configuration and private-network permission without exposing proxy credentials. These are configuration diagnostics, not an invisibility claim. `docs/Remote-files-and-transport.md` documents the API, buffering, cleanup and unsupported operations.

Independent base: `8819c284cb5b451ef0f369f660a326aed2571678`. Tested head: `d40b01a796fa2e73ae2f1285127b6406205dd05d`. This branch has no dependency on our attachment, interface, iframe, transport-selection or navigation patches.

## Validation

Rust 1.94.1, exact head above:
- Full `cargo nextest run --locked --offline --release --features render --no-fail-fast`: 1,707 passed, 4 skipped.
- CLI and worker release builds pass with render; render,stealth; no-default-features; no-default-features,stealth.
- Focused native API/IO release nextest: 8 passed with render/stealth, 7 without render/stealth, 8 with no-render/stealth. Includes status redaction, input rejection, chunk/range behavior, eviction, byte caps and release on close.
- Isolated direct and CONNECT-proxy TLS fixture: navigation and native PDF export share Chrome GREASE, cipher preference order and Windows Chrome 145 UA. Download cookies and proxy routing are observed on the receiver. The 45-byte exported fixture has SHA-256 `5b2ceb6997092fc8ed6d4900afaf2bb74cab0aee11f0fc63bd02121c35a9a550`.
- Full authenticated MCP download integration passes in direct mode: redirects/cookies, browser cookie synchronization, independent sessions and hostnames, saved client bytes/hash, HTTP/MIME/PDF validation, fixed/chunked/decompressed bounds, stream/artifact cleanup and expiry. Both TLS modes exercise native export; the full authenticated MCP integration was run in direct mode only.
- Original obstacle course `6ebac82`: 32/33 with the same reproduced baseline observer-fixture failure. Separately corrected fixture `3184db3`: 33/33. This does not claim the original suite is fully green.
- The custom API is absent on the frozen base and the adapter's mandatory capability check rejects it. The tested API branch satisfies that capability check without relaxing it.

## Rendering

Not applicable: no layout, paint or screenshot implementation changes.

## Performance

The unchanged upstream five-round interleaved harness passes its latency/RSS thresholds against frozen upstream, using matched render/stealth builds. DOM: 64.0 → 64.0 ms and 49.7 → 50.2 MiB. Storage: 15.6 → 15.7 ms and 37.1 → 37.3 MiB. These measurements cover ordinary DOM/storage overhead; the live transfer tests above establish bounded file behavior, not bulk-download throughput.

title: Use native stealth transport for scripts, forms and preflights
body:
## What changed

With a render/stealth build and `serve --stealth`, classic scripts, form POSTs and CORS preflights can still use the ordinary HTTP client. Route these operations through the installed native stealth client so their TLS and User-Agent identity agree with navigation, modules and rendering resources. Fixes #977.

Refreshed against upstream `4b7028830222175ca812a5caef04f9d802e64c23` on 2026-09-15, preserving the original PR history. The conflict with merged #974 is resolved by checking the selected transport's preflight status before CORS permission headers. Preserve #974's intermediate-redirect CORS checks and #968's redirect credential/body-header stripping in both transport paths.

**Validation caveat:** functional checks and all four build configurations pass, but the unchanged local performance smoke check fails its DOM latency threshold. The measurements and timing investigation below replace the old head's passing performance evidence. This refresh is not a claim that all merge gates pass.

Native OPTIONS requests follow no redirects, send no cookies/authorization (including configured extra headers), do not store response cookies, and preserve repeated permission headers. Form redirects preserve 307 bodies and rewrite 303 requests to GET; a connection reset never retries POST.

## Validation

Tested head: `34bfcb42924229173455dcc29dc6997f8d210a4e`, Linux x86_64, Rust 1.94.1, locked dependencies, release builds, two build jobs and incremental compilation disabled.

- Two new preflight regressions fail on original head `99622e9` and pass on this head: a 403 OPTIONS without CORS headers reports its HTTP status before checking permission, and no denied DELETE reaches the server. Both ordinary and stealth paths are covered. A third regression runs the intermediate-redirect CORS check with native stealth enabled.
- Focused render/stealth net and JS nextest: **37 passed**, including credential stripping, preflight permissions, form redirects/cookies and POST non-replay.
- Full release render nextest: **1,722 passed, 4 skipped**.
- CLI and worker release builds: render; render,stealth; no-default-features; no-default-features,stealth: **all passed**.
- Relevant no-render net and JS tests: **22 passed** without stealth; **35 passed** with stealth.
- Controlled direct and HTTP CONNECT-proxy TLS fixtures: **14 requests across 13 paths pass in each mode**, covering navigation, classic/modules/imports, styles/imports, images/background/font, fetch/XHR/preflight, form POST/redirect and screenshot completion. Every request has Chrome GREASE, the same cipher preference list and the Windows Chrome 145 UA; every proxied request matches an observed CONNECT connection. Credential/cookie assertions pass. Only the fixtures enable private networking and their temporary CA.
- Fresh upstream still fails the classic-script/preflight/form portions of that fixture. The independent PR probe reads the submitted document through raw CDP because the separate form-navigation utility-context repair is outside this PR. This does not claim to fix that navigation issue or provide the separate native-download CDP extension.
- Original obstacle course at `6ebac829`: **32/33 on both refreshed upstream and this head**, with the same observer-progression failure. The separately corrected fixture at `3184db3` gives **33/33** on this head. No benchmark modification is included.
- Policy: zero errors; one advisory warning because the regressions are in existing Rust test modules.

## Rendering

No layout or paint change relative to the refreshed upstream base. Resource loading and screenshot completion are exercised by the TLS fixture; no visual-fidelity claim.

## Performance

Compared fresh upstream `4b70288` with this head using the same compiler and feature configuration. The unchanged upstream five-round harness, using the render-only binaries configured by upstream CI, **fails**: DOM 114.7 to 164.9 ms (+43.8%); peak RSS 51.0 to 50.2 MiB. Storage is 32.0 to 32.0 ms (+0.3%), RSS 38.6 to 38.3 MiB. Correct results and resource limits pass.

DOM samples in milliseconds, in per-binary sampling order:

```text
base:      168.220, 114.700, 167.568, 64.433, 114.065
candidate: 164.896, 165.024, 166.222, 114.658, 114.131
```

The validation image uses Python 3.11.2. Its `Popen.wait(timeout=...)` polls with exponential delays capped at 50 ms, and the observed durations cluster near polling boundaries. A separate 15-round diagnostic retains the upstream scenarios, expected results, process-group cleanup, timeouts, resource limits and failure thresholds, but measures blocking process completion with a separate timeout watchdog. On the same render-only binaries, DOM is 132.6 to 135.2 ms (+1.9%, sample ranges 78.8–160.7 and 91.2–166.3 ms); storage is 26.7 to 29.6 ms (+10.9%, +2.9 ms), with RSS changes below 1%. title: fix(cdp): answer input events during a JS-triggered navigation instead of blocking
body:
## What changed

Fixes #921.

A CDP command that made the page schedule a document navigation (Enter in a form field, a click on a link or submit button) ran that navigation inline on the connection processor: for Enter `process_cdp_message` dispatched the synthetic `Page.navigate` right after the command's response, for `mouseReleased` the input handler awaited `process_pending_navigation()` inside the command. Either way the connection was not read until the new document had loaded, so the client's next command (usually the matching `keyUp` / `mouseReleased`, which Chromium answers in milliseconds) waited for the whole fetch and ran into client timeouts.

- `obscura-cdp/server.rs`: `process_cdp_message` returns the pending navigation instead of dispatching it; `cdp_processor` feeds it into `process_with_interception`, the spawn-and-defer loop `Page.navigate` and the runtime pump already use, so the processor keeps reading while the document loads and the frame events come from that loop. The synthetic `Page.navigate` (`synthetic_navigation`) carries the outgoing document's referrer (`__referrer`, computed before the page URL changes), so `document.referrer` after a link click or form submit is the source URL as before; automation `Page.navigate` keeps its empty referrer. The request method is taken from the document unchanged: a POST form without successful controls submits an empty POST instead of turning into a GET (the `Page.navigate` handler had the same `POST && !body.is_empty()` check and is fixed alike).
- Inside the interception loop, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`, `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, `Input.insertText` and `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` **whose session is the navigating target** are answered immediately with an empty result instead of being deferred. This is a deliberate, narrowly scoped divergence: Chromium would still dispatch such an event to the outgoing document, but Obscura cannot enter V8 from the processor while the navigation task owns the page's isolate, so the event is acknowledged and not executed. Input for every other target on the connection stays on the deferred path and runs after the navigation settles, exactly as before.
- `obscura-cdp/domains/input.rs`: `mouseReleased` leaves a document navigation pending (the processor picks it up as above) and reports a same-document move via `sync_virtual_url()` only when no document navigation is pending. The location setters preview their target in `__virtualUrl` before recording the navigation; syncing that preview produced an early `Page.frameNavigated` under the old loader id plus a history push before any document bytes. A link click now yields exactly one `Page.frameNavigated`, after the load, with the new loader id (as on `main` and in Chromium). The SPA case (`page_frame_contract.rs`) is unchanged.
- `obscura-browser/page.rs`: `navigate_with_wait_post_referrer` (method, body and referrer; `navigate_with_wait_post` delegates with an empty referrer), `has_pending_navigation` (peek without consuming), `document_referrer_for` (shared by `process_pending_navigation`, which is unchanged in behaviour).

No change to the runtime event loop or to rendering (the runtime gains a `has_pending_navigation` peek). No-render builds take the same path.

Not in this change: `Runtime.evaluate` / `Runtime.callFunctionOn` still run a navigation started from the evaluated expression inline (`domains/runtime.rs`); `cdp_click_submit_parity.rs` relies on that and it is a separate behaviour.

## Validation

New processor-level tests in `server.rs` with a local fixture whose `/slow` document answers after 1.5 s (each one fails with its fix reverted):

- `input_events_are_answered_while_js_triggered_navigation_is_in_flight` (Enter submit: `keyUp` answered in < 500 ms, `location.href` afterwards reports the result page; inline dispatch: `keyUp was blocked behind the navigation for 1.512s`)
- `mouse_released_on_link_is_answered_while_navigation_is_in_flight` (link click: `mouseReleased` answered in < 500 ms, navigation completes)
- `input_for_another_target_runs_after_the_navigating_target_settles` (tab A loads `/slow`, a native click in tab B still navigates B and the server sees B's request)
- `link_click_emits_one_frame_navigated_with_the_new_loader_id` (no `Page.frameNavigated` before the `mouseReleased` response, exactly one after the load, loader id differs from the initial one)
- `empty_post_form_submitted_by_click_stays_post` (server sees `POST /submit-empty`, never a GET)
- `link_click_navigation_carries_source_referrer` (`document.referrer` equals the source page URL)

```
cargo nextest run --release --features render --no-fail-fast -p obscura-cdp            # 194 passed, 3 skipped
cargo nextest run --release --no-default-features --no-fail-fast -p obscura-cdp       # 160 passed, 3 skipped
cargo nextest run --release --features render --no-fail-fast -p obscura-render -p obscura-js -p obscura-browser -p obscura-cdp   # 1356 passed, 4 skipped
cargo build --release -p obscura-cli --bins --no-default-features
cargo build --release -p obscura-cli --bins --features render,stealth
OBSCURA_BIN=target/release/obscura python3 obstacle-course/run.py --runs 1 --warmup 0   # 32/33 (observer-intersection fails identically on unpatched main)
```

Manual check (offline, loopback TLS origin + authenticated proxy, stealth build, result page delayed 10 s): Enter `keyUp` and link `mouseReleased` answered in 1 ms / 3 ms instead of timing out after 8 s; `Runtime.evaluate` sent next is deferred until the navigation ends (10 s) and reports the result page; a form whose action is unreachable leaves the old DOM with the committed target URL (pre-existing, unchanged).

## Rendering

Not a rendering change.

## Performance

No new work on the hot path: while a navigation is in flight every non-`Fetch.*` message is parsed once to see whether it is an input command of the navigating session (previously the same messages were parsed once when replayed). No memory change.

## Checklist

- [x] The change is focused and does not remove existing behavior without justification (input events of the navigating session during an in-flight navigation, also one started by `Page.navigate`, are acknowledged instead of replayed against the new document; scope and rationale stated above).
- [x] Tests cover the failure or feature.
- [x] Existing tests pass, including render and no-render configurations when affected.
- [x] I checked for CPU, latency, and memory regressions.
- [x] Public API or user-facing behavior changes are documented (`Page::navigate_with_wait_post_referrer`, `Page::has_pending_navigation`, `Page::document_referrer_for`; `process_cdp_message` now returns `Option<String>`, internal).

title: fix(js): resolve data:/blob: URLs and perform synchronous XHR
body:
Two independent fixes, one commit each. Both surfaced while automating a
production SPA that never reached its login screen under obscura but works in
headless Chrome.

Fixes #907
Fixes #908

## 1. `data:` and `blob:` resolve without the network (#907)

Dynamic `import()`, module scripts, `blob:` classic scripts and `fetch()` all
failed for URLs that carry their own payload. Two causes:

- **`validate_fetch_url`** rejected every scheme but `http`/`https`. Its comment
  only reasons about `file://`; `data:` and `blob:` look like collateral.
  Neither has a host to resolve and neither opens a socket, so the SSRF check
  below the gate has nothing to protect. `file://` stays rejected, and there is
  a test asserting that.
- **`ObscuraModuleLoader::load`** handed every specifier to the HTTP client with
  no scheme branch, so a `data:` module failed at the transport even once the
  gate passed.

`fetch("data:…")` is now answered inline — sending it to the transport produced
a reqwest *builder error* rather than a response. `blob:` bodies live in the JS
object-URL store, which the Rust loader cannot read, so `createObjectURL`
mirrors script sources into the page state and `revokeObjectURL` clears them.

#532 fixed the classic-script `data:` path and explicitly kept module scripts on
`import()`; this covers that remainder plus the `fetch` and `blob:` cases.

## 2. Synchronous XHR actually performs the request (#908)

`XMLHttpRequest.prototype.open` ignored its third argument and `send()` always
took the async `fetch` path, so a caller reading `xhr.status` on the next line
saw `0` with an empty body — no exception, no `error` event, indistinguishable
from a real network failure.

`open()` now records the async flag and `send()` routes the synchronous case
through a new `op_fetch_url_sync`. deno_core ops cannot block the isolate on the
page's own event loop, so the request runs on a dedicated thread with its own
current-thread runtime and the op waits for it — nothing on the page loop is
polled meanwhile, which is the observable semantics of a sync XHR. The op reuses
the same blocked-URL list, SSRF gate and `data:` handling as the async path.

## Verification

`cargo test --release -p obscura-js --lib` — **396 passed, 0 failed**.
All four release configurations build.

Behaviour matrix against a live `https://` document, compared with headless
Chrome (`PASS` = matches Chrome):

| case | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `import("data:…")` literal / base64 / percent-encoded | FAIL | PASS |
| `import("data:…")` with non-ASCII source | FAIL | PASS |
| `import(blob:…)` | FAIL | PASS |
| `<script src="data:…">` classic | PASS | PASS |
| `<script src="blob:…">` classic | FAIL | PASS |
| `<script type="module" src="data:…">` | FAIL | PASS |
| `fetch("data:…")` | FAIL | PASS |
| `fetch(blob:…)` | FAIL | PASS |
| `new Worker(blob:…)` | PASS | PASS |
| sync XHR, existing path | `status 0` | `status 200`, body present |
| sync XHR, missing path | `status 0` | `status 404`, `readyState 4` |
| async XHR (regression) | PASS | PASS |
| **`fetch("file://…")` rejected** | PASS | **PASS** |

15/15 on the combined matrix after the change.

## Notes for review

- The scheme allowance is deliberately narrow: `data:` and `blob:` only, added
  *before* the SSRF branch rather than widening the allow-list, so private-IP
  and `file://` handling is untouched.
- The sync path is opt-in per request; the async transport is unchanged.
- Mirroring blob sources into page state costs one string per script-typed
  object URL and is cleared on `revokeObjectURL`. If you would rather the loader
  reach into the JS store some other way, I am happy to rework it.
